stories.headline: Senate Budget Panel Chair Says No Funding for New Flood-Control Projects in 2027
stories.deck: The Senate budget panel signaled tighter scrutiny of flood-control spending after severe flooding and questions over project performance.
body: The chair of the Senate finance committee said no funding for new flood-control projects should be included in the 2027 national budget while the government reviews existing projects, implementation backlogs and the performance of flood-mitigation spending.
The position followed widespread flooding in Luzon and renewed scrutiny of Department of Public Works and Highways flood-control projects.
The proposed 2027 budget remains subject to committee hearings and plenary deliberations, where project-level allocations can still change.
A pause on new projects would shift attention toward completing, auditing and evaluating existing infrastructure before additional public funds are committed.

stories.headline: DOH Records 5,835 Leptospirosis Cases Nationwide as Flood Exposure Drives Recent Rise
stories.deck: DOH data cited by multiple reports show 5,835 cases and 358 deaths this year, while the recent case trend has risen after widespread flooding.
body: Department of Health data cited by multiple Philippine reports show 5,835 leptospirosis cases nationwide this year and 358 deaths.

Leptospirosis is a bacterial disease associated with exposure to water or soil contaminated by infected animal urine. Concern typically rises after severe flooding because residents, responders and commuters may have unavoidable contact with floodwater.
The current rise comes as many communities are still recovering from prolonged flooding, creating a second public-health burden on households and hospitals.

Watch for updated DOH surveillance data, local case clusters and hospital-capacity advisories. FMB News is using 358 deaths after the earlier conflicting figure was cross-checked against multiple current reports citing DOH data.

stories.headline: Project NOAH Head Says Decades of Ignoring 1941 Flood Plan Worsened Flood Risk
stories.deck: Mahar Lagmay called for science-based, system-wide flood planning rather than disconnected projects as severe flooding continued.
body: UP Resilience Institute executive director and Project NOAH head Mahar Lagmay said recurring flooding reflects decades of failure to follow a comprehensive flood-control master plan drafted in 1941.
The comments came as Metro Manila and parts of Luzon experienced prolonged flooding after repeated monsoon rain.
The policy question is whether national and local agencies will align future flood-control spending with updated science-based basin plans and transparent project evaluation.
He argued that flood mitigation should be treated as a connected watershed and drainage problem rather than as a collection of isolated projects.

stories.headline: Diesel and Kerosene Prices Drop by Nearly ₱4 per Liter as September Begins
stories.deck: The September 1 rollback provided motorists relief after two consecutive weeks of fuel-price increases.
body: Fuel retailers implemented price cuts effective 6 a.m. on September 1, with the largest reductions applied to diesel and kerosene.
The rollback followed two straight weeks of increases and reflected easing international oil-market pressure even as geopolitical risks remained.
Consumers should watch the next round of oil-company price advisories for whether the rollback is sustained or reversed as international oil-market conditions change.

Seaoil announced cuts of ₱0.32 per liter for gasoline, ₱3.83 for diesel and ₱3.84 for kerosene, while Petron and Shell cut gasoline by ₱0.30 and diesel and kerosene by ₱3.80. Unioil announced gasoline and diesel reductions of ₱0.40 and ₱3.90, respectively.

stories.headline: Army Officer Says His Unit Received No DepEd Confidential Funds for Youth Summits
stories.deck: Boransing said the Army funded its own participation and that his certification was not meant to validate DepEd's use of confidential funds.
body: Army Col. Manaros Boransing II testified during Day 20 of Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial that his unit did not receive confidential funds from the Department of Education for Youth Leadership Summit activities in 2023.
The prosecution questioned military certifications that appeared in DepEd's response to audit findings involving confidential-fund expenditures.

Boransing said the Army certification documented participation in the activities and was not intended to certify how DepEd spent its confidential funds. He said he had no personal knowledge of DepEd's funding source for the department's own participation.

The testimony bears on whether military activities cited in supporting documents actually received or used the confidential funds under scrutiny. It does not by itself determine liability in the impeachment case.

stories.headline: Palace Orders Alternative Government Work Arrangements in 15 Luzon Provinces
stories.deck: Essential and disaster-response services were required to continue operating while covered offices shifted to alternative arrangements.
body: Malacañang directed government agencies in 15 provinces in Northern and Central Luzon to adopt appropriate alternative work arrangements on September 1 because of expected heavy rainfall from the enhanced southwest monsoon.

The order was a weather-related continuity measure for national government offices rather than a blanket shutdown. It allowed agencies in the covered provinces to reduce travel exposure while keeping public functions available during a period of persistent Habagat rainfall and saturated conditions across parts of Luzon.

Residents and government personnel should rely on subsequent Palace, Civil Service Commission, NDRRMC and local government advisories for any extension, lifting or change in work arrangements as weather conditions evolve.
The directive was issued through Memorandum Circular No. 133 upon the recommendation of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council.
